court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: District Judge, Family Court, Thanjavur - H.M.O.P.No.187 of 2021
facts_of_case: The parties were married in 2012 and are living separately due to misunderstandings. The petitioner is seeking transfer of the case from Thanjavur to Tiruppur.

legal_principles.principle: Where the wife pleads lack of money, it has to be considered.
legal_principles.held: In the case of Geeta Heera vs. Harish Chander Heera [(2000) 10 SCC 304], the Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that where the petitioner's wife has pleaded lack of money, the same has to be considered.
cited_cases: Geeta Heera vs. Harish Chander Heera [(2000) 10 SCC 304]
use_in: divorce cases where wife's financial situation is relevant

legal_principles.principle: The court may transfer proceedings to a more convenient forum, considering the difficulties faced by the wife.
legal_principles.held: In the case of Mona Aresh Goel vs. Aresh Satya Goel [(2000) 9 SCC 255], when the wife pleaded that she was unable to bear the traveling expenses and even to travel alone and stay at Bombay, the Supreme Court ordered transfer of proceedings.
cited_cases: Mona Aresh Goel vs. Aresh Satya Goel [(2000) 9 SCC 255]
use_in: divorce cases where wife faces difficulties in traveling

legal_principles.principle: The court may consider the distance and difficulties faced by the wife in deciding a transfer petition.
legal_principles.held: In the case of Lalita A.Ranga vs. Ajay Champalal Ranga [(2000) 9 SCC 355], considering the distance and the difficulties faced by the wife, the Supreme Court has allowed the transfer petition.
cited_cases: Lalita A.Ranga vs. Ajay Champalal Ranga [(2000) 9 SCC 355]
use_in: divorce cases where wife faces difficulties in traveling

outcome.final_order: Transfer petition allowed, case transferred from Thanjavur to Tiruppur.

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo dat quod non habet
use_for_drafting: drafting a transfer petition in family court
advising on divorce and separation matters
